content.title: About
content.content: Fruit cheesecake is a dessert made from cream cheese, eggs, and sugar, topped with fresh or canned fruit. It has a smooth, creamy texture and the fruit layer adds natural sweetness and aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The earliest cheesecake recipes date back to ancient Greece, where they used cheese called feta.
The modern New York‑style cheesecake became popular in the early 20th century.
Fruits on cheesecake are often presented as a glaze, compote, or fresh slices.
Cheesecake can be made without baking, using a cookie‑butter crust.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Cream cheese is rich in calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Cheese and eggs provide complete protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and cheese contain vitamins B2 and B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants from fruit
items.content: Fresh berries and fruit supply vitamin C and polyphenols that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Probiotic effect
items.content: Certain cream cheeses (e.g., cottage cheese) contain live cultures that support gut microbiota.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar increase calories and can affect blood glucose levels.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cream cheese contains lactose, which may cause discomfort for lactose‑intolerant individuals.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: People allergic to milk or whey proteins should avoid cheesecake.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: Cream cheese is high in saturated fat, so portion control is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve cheesecake chilled, sliced into portions. Pair it with berry sauce, honey, or fresh fruit. For a lighter version, use low‑fat cottage cheese and sugar substitutes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cheesecake in the refrigerator at 2‑4 °C, covered with plastic wrap. Consume within 3‑5 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight container for up to 2 months.
